03560426.mechanism: 3-4 solid boxes (w 1-4, h 2-5, distinct colours) stand on the bottom row left to right with one-column gaps; the output re-stacks them as a top-left-anchored cascade where each next box's top-left cell sits on the previous box's bottom-right cell and overwrites it.
03560426.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 10x10 in and out; pair 0 boxes 888/77/222 span cols 0-9 (grid_col=11) and cascade shows 8877 overlap row, i.e. later box overwrites the shared corner.

dimensions.why: Canvas is common.grids(10, 10) and bounds 10/[10,11] are literals; the cascade and bottom-row layout only need sum(w)+n-1 <= W and sum(h)-(n-1) <= H, nothing in the rule references 10.

objects.why: Box count 3-4 and sizes w1-4/h2-5 are literals sized to a 10-wide row (incidental); solid rectangular boxes are rule-supported because the cascade overlap is defined by box corners. Height 1 is excluded without a visible rule reason.

placement.why: Bottom alignment and left-to-right order define the cascade order (rule-supported); line 42 forces the row to end at col 8 or 9, i.e. the boxes must nearly fill the width, which is a generator choice not required by the rule.

density_colours.why: random_colors gives distinct box colours, which keeps the overwritten corner cell visible as a colour change; with equal neighbouring colours the overlap would still be well defined but harder to read, so distinctness is a reasonable rule-support choice. Density follows from box sizes.

rule_parameters.why: The only rule parameters are the fixed down-right cascade offsets (w-1, h-1) and overwrite order, which define the task.

demonstration_context.why: Output is a deterministic function of one input; the corner-overwrite convention is visible in any pair with >=2 boxes. Factory program does not consult demonstrations.

03560426.proposal: Parameterise H,W (e.g. 5-30 each) and replace literals 10/[10,11] at lines 30, 35, 36, 42 with W/H; allow trailing empty columns and n boxes 2..k with w,h ranges scaled to W/H. Keep distinct colours and cascade semantics. Requires recertification.
03560426.uncertainties: Whether the original ARC intent requires the boxes to fill the row (line 42) is not established by 4 fixtures; allowing h=1 boxes changes cascade appearance (horizontal run) and should be checked against the verifier.

05a7bcf2.mechanism: Banded 30x30 scene: yellow (4) column stubs above a full blue (8) line at row 9-10, red (2) columns hanging up from row 19-23 in every column. Output: yellow stubs become green (3), yellow extends down to the 8 line, 8 continues to the far edge in those columns, and red bars in those columns slide to the far edge; flip/transpose give 4 orientations.
05a7bcf2.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 30x30; pair 0 is the transposed form (8 line at col 9) and shows red runs moved to col 29 only in stub rows.

dimensions.why: 30 is hardcoded in the canvas (53), the column loop bound (41), 30 dtalls (50), and loops (60, 63); band rows 9-10 and 19-23 (49) are literals. The projection rule needs only band order, not a 30 canvas.

objects.why: Stub groups width 2-5 and height <=3 and red heights 1-5 are literals (incidental); a red bar in every column (len-30 dtalls) is a generator choice; stubs as column groups are rule-supported because each stub column defines a projection lane.

placement.why: Ordering yellow-above-8-above-red is the rule; absolute rows 0-7/9-10/19-23 are incidental to 30. flip/xpose cover only 4 orientations, the rest come from augmentation.

density_colours.why: Fixed role colours 4/3/8/2 are the task's semantic roles; palette changes belong to the augmentation layer. Density is set by stub and bar counts.

rule_parameters.why: Extend-to-8, continue-8-to-edge and slide-red-to-edge (offset 29) are the rule itself; no hidden parameter.

demonstration_context.why: Orientation is visible from the 8 line in the query; no demonstration-only parameter. Factory does not reference demonstrations.

05a7bcf2.proposal: Introduce independent H (band axis) and W (lane axis), place the 8 line at a sampled row with room above for stubs and below for red bars, and replace literal 29/30 with H-1/H, W. Optionally let some columns have no red bar. Recertify.
05a7bcf2.uncertainties: Minimum band heights needed so that slid red bars never collide with the extended 8 run were not derived; whether red bars may be absent in a stub column is not shown by fixtures.

0a1d4ef5.mechanism: 30x30 noise background (two random colours mixed 50/50 with black) containing a jittered lattice of solid boxes, always 3 columns by 2-4 rows; output is the lattice of box colours (3 wide, 2-4 tall).
0a1d4ef5.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs: inputs all 30x30, outputs 2x3, 3x3, 3x3, 4x3 (always 3 columns).

dimensions.why: Input canvas fixed at 30x30 (60, 72, 74) and output width fixed by randint(3, 3) with column cell length 8 (29, 31). Reading box colours into a lattice works for any lattice shape that fits; fixtures show only 3 columns but that is finite evidence.

objects.why: Boxes are solid and at least 3x3 so they stand out from noise (rule-supported); upper sizes length-1/depth-1 come from the fixed cell lattice (incidental).

placement.why: A row/column lattice topology is required for the output to be well defined; fixed 8-wide cells and 6-10 tall rows with offset 3 are literals.

density_colours.why: Box colours exclude noise colours (rule-supported). Noise density fixed at ~50% black (61). The intended 'no solid 3x3 noise patch' check indexes bgcolors with the box-lattice width (68) instead of 30, so it does not test the canvas; adjacent-distinct box colours (53-55) are not required by the rule.

rule_parameters.why: Output cell = box colour at the lattice position; no free rule parameter.

demonstration_context.why: Output determined by the query alone; factory does not consult demonstrations.

0a1d4ef5.proposal: Sample canvas H,W (e.g. 12-30) and lattice rows/cols 1-4 each with cell sizes derived from available space; fix the noise-patch check to index (r*W+c) over the actual canvas; optionally vary noise density. Recertify; check the verifier extracts lattices of other widths.
0a1d4ef5.uncertainties: Whether the verifier/factory assumes 3 output columns was not inspected; the probability of an accidental solid noise patch >=3x3 under the broken check is small (~(1/4)^9 per location) but nonzero.

0b17323b.mechanism: 15x15 canvas with exactly three colour-1 dots on the main diagonal at spacing 2-4 starting at 0 or 1; output continues the progression with colour 2 until the edge.
0b17323b.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, all 15x15, spacings 4/2/3 with starts 0/1/0; audit saw only 6 unique inputs in 128 samples, which is the whole native domain (3 spacings x 2 starts).

dimensions.why: Canvas and loop bound are literal 15; continuing a diagonal progression works on any canvas, including non-square ones where the diagonal ends at the shorter side.

objects.why: Exactly three given dots (num < 3) is a literal; two dots would already fix the step, so three is a demonstration-friendly choice rather than a rule necessity.

placement.why: Start restricted to 0/1 on the main diagonal and spacing 2-4; any start offset along the diagonal would preserve the rule. Anti-diagonal and other orientations come only from D4 augmentation.

density_colours.why: Two role colours (1 given, 2 predicted) on black are the task semantics.

rule_parameters.why: Step 2-4 is a literal; larger steps fit larger canvases provided at least one continuation dot exists.

demonstration_context.why: The query reveals its own step; no demonstration-only parameter. Factory does not consult demonstrations.

0b17323b.proposal: Sample H,W independently, a start offset s >= 0, a step d, and k=3 (optionally 2-4) given dots subject to at least one continuation fitting in min(H,W). This lifts the 6-input domain substantially. Recertify.
0b17323b.uncertainties: Whether the factory/verifier assumes the progression starts at the corner (0/1) was not inspected; varying the number of given dots changes evidence strength and needs a check that step remains identifiable.

0becf7df.mechanism: 10x10 with a 2x2 legend [[a,b],[c,d]] in the top-left corner and one connected figure built from random strokes of legend colours; output swaps a<->b and c<->d inside the figure, legend unchanged.
0becf7df.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 10x10, legend at (0..1, 0..1) in every pair; each figure uses all four legend colours.

dimensions.why: Canvas literal 10 and stroke ranges 0-7/1-6/0-5/1-8 are tied to 10; legend lookup is position-based in the corner and would work on any canvas >= ~5.

objects.why: Single connected figure from >=10 strokes is a generator style (incidental); requiring all five colours present (32) is rule-supported because every swap pair must be evidenced.

placement.why: Legend fixed at the top-left corner is the task convention (augmentation moves it); figure confined to cols 2-9 and kept off cells (0..2, 2) to separate it from the legend, which is rule-supporting.

density_colours.why: Four distinct legend colours are necessary for two unambiguous swap pairs; figure colours drawn from legend plus black.

rule_parameters.why: The swap pairs are the legend rows; this is the rule.

demonstration_context.why: Pairing along legend rows (not columns) is a convention that demonstrations must disambiguate, and transpose augmentation flips it, so episodes must use one consistent D4 transform; the factory hardcodes it rather than reading demonstrations.

0becf7df.proposal: Parameterise H,W (e.g. 6-30) and scale stroke ranges and the figure region to the canvas; keep the corner legend and separation gap. Recertify.
0becf7df.uncertainties: Whether figures that do not touch the legend gap or multiple disconnected figures are acceptable to the verifier was not inspected.

0e671a1a.mechanism: 13x13 with three single pixels colours 2, 4, 3 in distinct rows and columns; output draws grey (5) L-paths 2->4 then 4->3, each moving horizontally first then vertically.
0e671a1a.fixture_evidence: 5 canonical pairs, all 13x13; pair 0 shows row-10 horizontal run then col-1 vertical run from 2 to 4, then row-1 run and col-11 run from 4 to 3.

dimensions.why: range(1, 12) and grids(13, 13) are literals; L-path routing is canvas-agnostic.

objects.why: Exactly three role pixels 2/4/3 form the chain the rule connects; more points would be a different rule.

placement.why: Distinct rows and columns (sample without replacement) prevent paths overrunning other pixels and degenerate straight paths, which supports the rule; excluding the border rows/cols 0 and 12 is not required.

density_colours.why: Colour roles 2,3,4 and path colour 5 encode chain order; recolouring is augmentation-level.

rule_parameters.why: Chain order (0,2),(2,1) and horizontal-then-vertical turn are fixed conventions of the task.

demonstration_context.why: The horizontal-first convention and chain order are not inferable from the query alone; demonstrations supply them, and transpose augmentation turns them into vertical-first, so a whole episode must share one transform.

0e671a1a.proposal: Sample H,W independently (e.g. 5-30) and pixel rows/cols from the full range including borders while keeping distinct rows/cols. Recertify.
0e671a1a.uncertainties: Whether border pixels change any verifier assumption was not checked.

0f63c0b9.mechanism: 15x15 with 3-4 pixels in rows separated by >=2; output draws a full row line at each pixel row, colours the left/right borders by nearest pixel row (ties to the upper pixel), and the top/bottom border rows with the first/last colour.
0f63c0b9.fixture_evidence: 5 canonical pairs, all 15x15; pair 0 rows 3/7/12 show gap rows 4-5 coloured 2 and row 6 coloured 7, i.e. the odd-gap middle row goes to the upper pixel.

dimensions.why: A size parameter exists (20) and drives the loops, but the canvas is still grids(15, 15) at line 38, so size != 15 would be inconsistent; width and height are not independent. The rule (row lines + nearest-row borders) is size-agnostic.

objects.why: 3-4 pixels is a literal; 2 or more pixels with row gaps >1 keep the rule well defined.

placement.why: Row gaps >1 (36) are rule-supporting (each border segment exists); columns limited to 3..size-4 have no effect on the output and are incidental; rows exclude the outer rows.

density_colours.why: Distinct pixel colours are required so border segments are attributable.

rule_parameters.why: Nearest-row split with upper-wins tie and top/bottom border colours are the rule.

demonstration_context.why: The odd-gap tie-break (upper pixel wins) is only demonstrated when some pair has an odd gap; vertical-flip augmentation inverts it, so episodes need a consistent transform and should include an odd gap. Whether sampled episodes guarantee that was not checked.

0f63c0b9.proposal: Use independent H,W (replace 15 at line 38 and use H for rows, W for columns), sample 2-k pixels with row gaps >=2 and columns from the full width. Consider an episode-level requirement that at least one demonstration has an odd gap. Recertify.
0f63c0b9.uncertainties: Episode assembly behaviour for the tie-break evidence is not inspected; the archived verifier's handling of other sizes is unverified.

11dc524f.mechanism: 13x13 orange (7) background with a fixed 2x2 grey square at row 6 col 4 and a 2-3 x 2-3 diagonally connected red sprite on one of four sides; output slides the sprite to touch the square's side and replaces the square with the sprite's mirror image (grey) across the contact edge.
11dc524f.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 13x13 with the grey square at rows 6-7, cols 4-5 in every pair; sprites 2x3 or 3x3. Audit: 114 unique inputs in 128.

dimensions.why: Canvas 13 and every coordinate literal (8, 6, 4, 10, 13) assume the fixed square; slide-and-mirror does not depend on canvas size.

objects.why: The grey square is always exactly 2x2 at one position (48), incidental; sprite size 2-3 is a literal. A diagonally connected sprite is rule-supporting so the mirror is a single readable shape.

placement.why: Sprite must overlap the square's row/column span so the slide lands on it (rule-supported); fixed square location and literal ranges are incidental.

density_colours.why: Role colours 7 background, 2 sprite, 5 square/mirror encode the task.

rule_parameters.why: Direction is chosen by the side (angle) and the mirror is across the contact edge; the four cases are the rule.

demonstration_context.why: Side is visible in the query; no demonstration-only parameter. Factory does not consult demonstrations.

11dc524f.proposal: Parameterise H,W, the grey square's position and size (e.g. 1-4 per side) and sprite sizes up to ~5, recomputing the side ranges from these values. Recertify.
11dc524f.uncertainties: Whether the mirror is meant to match the square's size (2x2 square vs 3-tall mirror in fixtures) means square size may be irrelevant; whether the verifier keys on a 2x2 square was not checked.

1478ab18.mechanism: 8x8 orange background with four grey corner pixels of a square of side 4-8, one corner nudged one cell diagonally inward (the dog-ear); output draws an azure right triangle whose legs run along the dog-eared corner's row and column and whose hypotenuse is the square's diagonal, with grey points kept on top.
1478ab18.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 8x8; sides 4/6/8/7 and all four dog-ear corners appear across train+test. Audit: 79 unique inputs, 30 orbits; the whole native domain is 220 scenes (sum over sides 4-8 of (9-L)^2 x 4).

dimensions.why: Canvas literal 8 and side <= 8 come from the canvas, not the rule; a dog-eared square works on any H,W >= side.

objects.why: A square is rule-supported because the hypotenuse is a 45-degree diagonal (51) joining opposite corners; side >= 3 is needed so the nudged corner is not another corner. The 4 lower bound and 8 upper bound are literals.

placement.why: Square position is any offset inside the 8x8 canvas; nothing in the rule fixes it, so a larger canvas would give more positions and margins.

density_colours.why: Background 7, marker 5 and fill 8 are role colours; recolouring is augmentation-level.

rule_parameters.why: All four dog-ear corners are sampled, covering every case of the rule.

demonstration_context.why: Which legs are drawn is a convention, but it is a fixed function of the visible dog-ear; demonstrations only need to show it. Factory does not consult demonstrations.

1478ab18.proposal: Sample H,W independently (e.g. 4-30), side 3..min(H,W), and any offset. This lifts a 220-scene finite domain. Optionally allow non-square rectangles only if the verifier is shown to define a non-45-degree hypotenuse (not recommended). Recertify.
1478ab18.uncertainties: Side 3 (nudged corner becomes the centre) has not been checked against the verifier; whether the original rule draws a pixel diagonal on non-square boxes is unknown.

14b8e18c.mechanism: 10x10 orange background with 2-5 same-colour shapes: hollow rectangles, or diagonals when square; only hollow squares get eight red 'ear' pixels just outside their corners in the output. Non-square rectangles, diagonals and length-8 bars are distractors.
14b8e18c.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 10x10; pair 0 has a 4x4 hollow square with ears plus 2x2 diagonals and a 4x2 rectangle without ears; pair 2 nests a 2x2 square inside an 8x8 square.

dimensions.why: Canvas literal 10 and the length-8 special case (79-80) are tied to 10; ears and square detection are size-agnostic.

objects.why: Distinguishing squares from non-squares and hollow from diagonal is the rule (rule-supported); 2-5 shapes and sides 1-4 (plus 8) are literals.

placement.why: A clear background ring around each shape and non-colliding, in-canvas ears are required for the ears to be unambiguous.

density_colours.why: One shape colour excluding 2 and 7, and red ears, are role colours.

rule_parameters.why: The eight ear offsets are fixed by the rule.

demonstration_context.why: At least one square per scene (70) means every pair demonstrates ears; the square-only criterion is learnt from contrasts across pairs. Factory does not consult demonstrations.

14b8e18c.proposal: Parameterise H,W and replace the literal 8 with a 'long bar' length drawn relative to the canvas. Also move num_boxes and colour inside the rejection loop or bound it: the audit attempted only 43 draws (41 valid, 2 TimeoutErrors) in its time budget, so the sampled 41 unique inputs reflect slowness, not domain size. Recertify.
14b8e18c.uncertainties: Acceptance rate of the rejection loop at 5 boxes was not measured; whether nested squares (pair 2) remain well handled on larger canvases is unverified.

15113be4.mechanism: Square canvas (23 natively) split by yellow lines every 4 into 3x3 cells of random 1/0 noise; an 8x8 yellow-framed key in one corner shows a 3x3 sprite at 2x scale. Every cell whose 1-pixels cover the sprite's mask gets those pixels recoloured with the sprite colour; 2-4 matches required.
15113be4.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 23x23; pair 0 shows the key in the bottom-right corner (flip+flop) and three recoloured cells. Configured path adds approved square sizes 12/15/24/27 (5 shapes in 128 configured samples).

dimensions.why: Cell size 3 with spacing 3 matches the 3x3 sprite (rule-supported), and the 8x8 key frame is fixed by the 2x scaled sprite; but the canvas is square (34) with default 23, and nothing in the rule ties height to width.

objects.why: Sprite is a 3x3 mask with 3-5 filled cells (33); the 3x3 grain is intrinsic, the fill count limits are a sampling choice that keeps the match count in range.

placement.why: Lattice positions are fixed by the line spacing (rule-supported); the key is always in a corner, moved by flip/flop only.

density_colours.why: Noise is a fixed 50% Bernoulli per pixel (69); sprite colour excludes 1 and 4 (role-supported). Noise density does not affect the rule.

rule_parameters.why: The match test (all mask pixels are 1) is the rule; 2-4 matches is a guard so evidence exists without saturating, not a rule necessity.

demonstration_context.why: The key in the query defines the sprite; no demonstration-only parameter. Factory does not consult demonstrations.

15113be4.proposal: Allow independent H,W (each 4k-1 or with partial trailing cells, as the approved 12/24 overrides already do) instead of a single size; optionally vary noise density. Lower priority because the configured path already has five sizes.
15113be4.uncertainties: Whether non-square canvases or keys in non-corner positions are admissible to the verifier was not checked; acceptance of the 2-4 match guard at small sizes was not measured.

1b8318e3.mechanism: Grey 2x2 boxes and scattered coloured pixels; each pixel moves to the nearest cell of the ring around a box (Manhattan reach <= 4), with greedy uniqueness matching; ambiguous canonical cases are resolved by hand-coded overrides (extra_idxs).
1b8318e3.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs: three 15x15 and one 10x10, with 5-12 pixels; train pair 0 needs the extra_idxs override (validate line 104). The audit obtained 1 valid sample in 3 attempts with 2 TimeoutErrors, so its 10x10-only statistic is an artefact of one sample.

dimensions.why: Only square sizes 10 or 15 (5*base) are drawn; docking is defined for any H,W. Fixtures show both 10 and 15, so fixed 10x10 in the audit is a sampling artefact, not a constructor property.

objects.why: num_pixels = size..3*size (86) is far above the canonical 5-12 pixels (fixture 15x15 pair has 12 < 15), which makes every pixel needing a unique dock rarely satisfiable; this lower bound is incidental. 2x2 boxes are the rule's object.

placement.why: Box spacing 2 (84), reach <= 4 (52) and unique nearest site (56, 60) are rule-supporting; uniform random pixel positions are incidental and drive rejection.

density_colours.why: Pixel density ties to canvas size and is too high relative to fixtures; colours exclude grey 5 (role-supported).

rule_parameters.why: The docking tie-break is greedy by distance plus hand overrides for canonical pairs, so the generator's rule is not a complete specification of the original; the factory chooses among several docking rules using demonstrations.

demonstration_context.why: Factory solve() filters candidate docking RULES by consistency with demonstrations and raises Undetermined if the query is ambiguous, so episodes must contain pairs that discriminate rules; whether sampled episodes do so was not checked.

1b8318e3.proposal: Highest-priority fix is feasibility, not canvas size: sample num_pixels near fixture counts (e.g. 3..2*num_boxes+4) and place pixels within reach of a box, then sample independent H,W. Bound the rejection loop. Re-run the audit before judging diversity. Recertify.
1b8318e3.uncertainties: Which docking explanation the original intends for ties is unresolved (overrides exist); acceptance after the proposed change is unmeasured; the native constructor may currently be close to unusable for fresh sampling.

1c02dbbe.mechanism: 15x15 with a large grey rectangle; at up to four corners a colour marks the corner cell plus two pixels just outside the rectangle that give a sub-rectangle's width and height; output fills each corner sub-rectangle with its colour inside the grey, without overlap.
1c02dbbe.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 15x15; grey rectangles 11x11, 10x10, 12x13, 13x13. The 10x10 grey rectangle of train pair 1 is outside the native range 11-13 (line 62).

dimensions.why: Canvas literal 15 and grey size 11-13 exclude a demonstrated 10x10 case; the corner-marker rule only needs a 1-cell margin around the grey rectangle.

objects.why: Up to four corner rectangles of 1-8 per side that must not overlap (57) are rule-supporting; the 1-8 bounds are literals tied to the grey size.

placement.why: Markers sit on the corner and just outside the rectangle sides, so a >=1 margin is required; the rectangle anchors at the corners by definition.

density_colours.why: Distinct non-grey corner colours, each corner present with probability 1/2 and at least one present; the grey 5 role is fixed.

rule_parameters.why: Sub-rectangle size is read from marker offsets; no hidden parameter.

demonstration_context.why: All parameters are visible in the query. No direct factory exists; evidence is a direct-source certificate.

1c02dbbe.proposal: Sample canvas H,W independently, grey rectangle 3..H-2 by 3..W-2 with a >=1 margin, and corner sub-rectangle sizes up to the grey dimensions (non-overlap check retained). This covers the 10x10 fixture case. Recertify.
1c02dbbe.uncertainties: Edge cases where a marker pixel coincides with another corner's marker (w or h equal to the grey size) were not analysed; the certificate is a direct-source certificate whose program-hash freshness was not rebuilt here.

1d0a4b61.mechanism: 25x25 periodic mosaic of a D2-symmetric tile with a 1-coloured frame (period (h-1, w-1), tile 3-10 per side) with five random black rectangles erased; output restores the mosaic.
1d0a4b61.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 25x25, tiles 8x8, 7x7, 5x3 etc.; colours always include 1, 2, 5 plus one more.

dimensions.why: Canvas literal 25 is not required by periodic completion; tile size is broadly variable (35-36).

objects.why: Exactly five holes of 2-6 per side are literals; any number of holes works if every tile cell keeps a visible copy.

placement.why: Holes never touch row/col 0 or the last two rows/cols (1..23-size); not required by the rule. The generator does not check that each tile cell retains an unerased copy.

density_colours.why: Palette is fixed 1, 5, 2 plus one random colour, with 1 as the frame colour; periodic completion would work with any non-zero palette.

rule_parameters.why: Tile period is broad, but the tile is always mirror-symmetric in both axes; symmetry adds redundancy for completion and is a fixture trait, not proven necessary.

demonstration_context.why: The query contains enough periods to infer the tile; no demonstration-only parameter. Factory does not consult demonstrations.

1d0a4b61.proposal: Sample H,W independently (period multiples not required), hole count and sizes scaled to the canvas, and a free palette; add an explicit recoverability check (each tile cell has a visible copy, using symmetry only if the verifier relies on it). Recertify.
1d0a4b61.uncertainties: Whether the verifier uses symmetry or only periodicity is not inspected; the current generator could in principle erase all copies of a tile cell (not measured).

1d61978c.mechanism: 16x16 orange background with 2-7 separated grey diagonal segments of distinct lengths in both orientations; output colours every segment of the orientation with the larger total pixel count azure (8) and the other orientation red (2).
1d61978c.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, all 16x16. Train 0: '\' total 16 vs '/' 9, so '\' is 8; train 1: '\' 14 vs '/' 15, so '/' is 8. A fixed orientation-to-colour map therefore does not fit the fixtures; the majority-by-pixels rule does.

dimensions.why: Canvas literal 16 and candidate ranges 17-length/16 are tied to the canvas; segment colouring is size-agnostic.

objects.why: Distinct lengths (29, commented 'not a huge deal') and 2-10 lengths/2-7 segments are sampling choices; diagonal segments are the rule's object.

placement.why: No segment may touch another within 2 cells orthogonally or at its ends; this keeps segments separable, which the rule needs (a looser clearance would still work, but some separation is required).

density_colours.why: Roles 7 background, 5 input segments, 8/2 output classes are fixed by the task.

rule_parameters.why: Both orientations present, near-equal segment counts and unequal pixel totals make the majority comparison well defined and stop segment counting from substituting for pixel counting.

demonstration_context.why: Telling 'majority orientation -> 8' apart from a fixed orientation map needs demonstrations whose majority orientations differ; nothing in the constructor or factory requires that within an episode (the factory does not read demonstrations).

1d61978c.proposal: Parameterise H,W (e.g. 8-30) and scale length bounds to min(H,W); keep the separation and majority constraints. Consider an episode-level check that both majority orientations occur among demonstrations. Recertify.
1d61978c.uncertainties: Episode-level orientation mix was not measured; the bounded packing (1000 attempts, RuntimeError) acceptance on small canvases is unknown.

1e81d6f9.mechanism: 15x15 sparse noise (each cell non-zero with probability 1/10, colours 1-9) with a grey L frame isolating a 3x3 key corner whose centre holds the target colour; output erases every target-coloured pixel outside the key.
1e81d6f9.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 15x15, key at top-left; pair 0 target 4 erased at four places.

dimensions.why: Canvas literal 15 (15*15 cells); erasing one colour is size-agnostic.

objects.why: Single pixels of random colours with at least one target pixel present (34), so every pair shows an erase.

placement.why: Key fixed at the corner with a grey L frame is the task layout; D4 augmentation moves it.

density_colours.why: Noise density fixed at 10%; any density with the target present works. Target excludes grey 5 (29) to keep the frame role.

rule_parameters.why: Single erase-target rule; target colour is read from the key.

demonstration_context.why: Target visible in the query key; factory does not consult demonstrations.

1e81d6f9.proposal: Sample H,W independently (key needs >= 4x4) and noise density (e.g. 5-25%). Recertify.
1e81d6f9.uncertainties: Noise colour 5 can appear outside the frame; whether the verifier treats grey noise adjacent to the frame as part of it was not checked.

20fb2937.mechanism: 20x11 input: header of three 3x3 coloured boxes with a key pixel colour under each, a magenta separator row 6, then a 13x11 region of single pixels; output (13x11) replaces each pixel with a 3x3 box of the mapped colour centred on it.
20fb2937.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, all 20x11 -> 13x11 with 8-9 boxes. The audit hit its 16 s profile budget after 76 valid draws (no errors): the unbounded overlap rejection at lines 33-37 for 8-9 boxes in an 11x9 origin range is slow.
